claim: NIG-TimeNet v2 default encoder (InstanceNorm on each feature window, ~900k parameters, dropout 0.1, effectively zero weight decay) on 1d relative-direction/magnitude targets
universe: 47 assets local, 222 assets Drive (89k train samples)
failure_location: model input: per-window InstanceNorm erases the feature level
evidence: Drive 222 assets: best epoch 5, test AUC 0.631/0.537 (mag/dir) falling to 0.608/0.528 at the end while train rises to 0.742/0.660; shuffled labels fitted (train 0.593/0.570 vs linear 0.507/0.512); 8 assets (~4k-13k samples) train 0.77-0.81 vs test 0.575-0.584. Linear probe (47 assets, test AUC mag/dir): raw levels 0.594/0.531, post-InstanceNorm view the transformer sees 0.522/0.521, stats path 0.628/0.536
verified_cause: InstanceNorm erases the feature level, which is where the (cross-sectional, volatility-level) signal lives, so memorization becomes the only way to lower train loss
cause_test: linear probe on the view the encoder sees vs raw levels (0.52 vs 0.59); fix (level passthrough + BatchNorm + GRU, 'RL_gru') moved the diagnostic as predicted: test 0.645/0.555 vs linear 0.609/0.538, train-test gap 0.014/0.016, shuffled-label fit at the linear level (0.508/0.518); controls present: shuffled labels, linear baseline, 8-coin vs 222-coin data size, noise floor +-0.005 AUC
invariants: any encoder that normalizes each window per feature without passing the level to the head loses the cross-sectional level signal and then memorizes; weight_decay was a no-op (AdamW multiplies it by lr)
reopen_if: R1: only if feature levels reach the head through another channel (the old config is not to be re-run as is)

claim: Architecture/capacity variants on top of the level fix for 1d relative direction: FiLM, coin embedding, twin towers (concat/gate), TCN, tiny capacity, width x8 / depth x2, cross-sectional rank features (xrank)
universe: 8 assets (4k-13k samples) and 222 Drive assets (89k train / 177k test)
failure_location: direction AUC ceiling ~0.55 independent of encoder and capacity
evidence: 8 assets: no variant consistently above the linear reference 0.592/0.529 (RL_film 0.604/0.515, RL_coin 0.588/0.523, 2tower 0.579/0.525, TCN 0.593-0.604/0.522-0.530; TCN first 'win' not repeated by seeds). 222 assets: RL_gru 0.645/0.555 vs linear 0.609/0.538 and linear+xrank 0.648/0.552 (GRU=linear on ranks); other encoders 0.638-0.645 mag, 0.549-0.552 dir (<=0.008 apart, noise floor +-0.005). Capacity sweep d_model 32..256 and 4 layers: test mag 0.639-0.643 and dir 0.545-0.553 flat (dir falls to 0.544-0.546 for larger) while train dir rises 0.561->0.608. xrank on 8 assets raises memorization (shuffled-label train 0.62/0.61 vs 0.55/0.56)
verified_cause: direction AUC is limited by the information in the 18 price/volume features, not by model capacity or encoder type
cause_test: capacity sweep (width x8, depth x2) leaves test flat while train rises; a linear model on cross-sectional rank features equals the GRU; sample-size comparison (8 vs 222 assets) and shuffled-label controls present
invariants: 1d relative-direction AUC ~0.55 and magnitude AUC ~0.645 for any encoder on the 18 OHLCV-derived features of 222 coins; encoder choice is within 0.008 AUC
reopen_if: R1: a new information source (funding/OI/intraday features; the archives were empty then) | R2: fair coin-embedding test with every coin in train (not run) | R3: feature-count sweep k=1..18 not yet run

claim: Trained NIG-TimeNet (relative target, crypto_model_v1_relative_am, best epoch 12) rank signal traded as a market-neutral daily long/short portfolio
period: test 79 days, then re-split with test 267 days (2025-12-25..2026-09-17)
failure_location: portfolio P&L: median-ordered rank vs mean returns with positive jump tails
evidence: rank signal real: daily IC of p_up_close 0.093 (t=11.9), AUC close 0.543 vs linear 0.536, permutation p=0.001; but net: val-chosen short-weakest-5% +0.077%/day [-0.17,+0.33] Sharpe 0.73 (not significant), chicks all coins daily -7.1%, rank portfolio gross -0.027%/day (net -0.047%/day t=-0.9); gross +0.054%/day < 0.08% cost; Sharpe 2.58 on 79 days was period luck. Clipping returns at +-10% turns the rank portfolio to +0.228%/day (t=5.7). Jump >20% next day: 5.07% in lowest p_up decile vs 0.17% in highest; median return rises with rank, mean is non-monotonic
verified_cause: the model ranks the median (volatile coins with negative median look like losers) while mean returns are dominated by positive jump tails in those same coins
cause_test: clipping at +-10% flips the rank portfolio from -0.027% to +0.228%/day (t=5.7); jump-rate by p_up decile 5.07% -> 0.17% and by uncertainty decile 0.21% -> 5.76%; volnorm target and stop-loss variants did not fix it (see F-0033)
invariants: rank IC ~0.09 is stable across val/test with no memorization (train-test gap ~0.01), but the net daily rank portfolio at 0.08% cost is <= 0 for every construction tried (extreme weights, vol-scaled, model+tree, stops)
reopen_if: R1: a construction that can capture the clipped-tail ranking (tail-hedged / long-only convex payoff) shown net > 0 on val before test | R2: information that predicts jump tails (funding/OI crowding; archives empty at the time)

claim: Daily +5% take-profit / -5% stop bracket on NIG-TimeNet p_up_close rank deciles: does the rank carry direction information?
period: test 2025-12-25..2026-09-17; double-touch days resolved from Binance hourly candles (96%)
evidence: share of resolved days where +5% was touched first: lowest p_up decile 50.8%, decile 5 54.7%, highest 52.2% (all coins 52.9%) - flat; touch frequency of either barrier falls 87% -> 29% with decile (volatility ordering); all strategies lose on test and val-selected ones are worse than random picks (short q=0.05 -0.200%/trade vs random -0.114%, p=0.98; q=0.1 worse by 0.04-0.05%, p=0.95-0.99). Later audit: IC inside prior-volatility quintiles 0.082 (t=12.2), partial after volatility rank 0.074 (t=10.6)
verified_cause: the rank orders volatility, not direction at the +-5% scale (ordinary-move ordering survives volatility control but gives no first-touch direction)
cause_test: first-touch up-share by decile (flat 50.8-54.7%) with touch-rate monotone in decile, against 300 random same-day selections; volnorm model gives the same picture (51.6% -> 50.7%)
invariants: no direction information at the +-5% scale in the 1d relative rank signal
reopen_if: R1: a barrier scale or horizon where first-touch up-share varies by >= 5 points across deciles with a pre-registered selection rule | R2: new information source (funding/OI)

claim: Direction rule built by combining the heads of the trained entry_range model (crypto_model_v1_entry_range_s100_am): 13 rules x 8 uncertainty gates x 5 coverages (M=520) frozen on val, scored once on test
universe: 83 coins (81 in val/test), 1h windows 32 bars stride 8
cost_model: maker 0.02% / taker 0.05%, worst-case intrabar order on 1h
failure_location: rule accuracy vs majority class; net P&L
evidence: val best by accuracy (p_hl inverted + high-epistemic gate) 0.4565, t=-2.69, Bonferroni x520 p=1.0, permutation p=0.345; test 0.490 (t=-0.83) vs majority 0.527. IC-best rule (p_mean inverted) IC 0.049 (t=8.9) but accuracy 0.496. Natural close head pc: acc 0.514, AUC 0.505. Partial IC after controlling last-candle return 0.003-0.013 (after -RSI14 ~0.03); -RSI14 alone IC 0.057 (t=9.1). Tradability test: first rule net -8.1bp/trade (t=-1.97, 3/9 months positive), gross -1.1bp, optimistic bound +5.1bp; at 5% coverage net -20.1bp; market-order entry -14.1bp. Heads high/low predict expansion (AUC ~0.74), not direction
verified_cause: the per-timestamp ranking IC of these rules is short-term reversal rediscovered, not a new direction signal from combining heads
cause_test: incremental.py: partial IC of each rule after controlling last-candle return collapses to 0.003-0.013 (asym 0.003, p_mean inverted 0.013); -RSI14 alone exceeds the rules
invariants: no gross margin before fees (-1 to -16 bp) while fees alone are ~7 bp; cross-sectional ranking among coins in one stamp does not give absolute direction (majority class 0.527)
reopen_if: R1: a rule whose partial IC after last-candle-return and RSI control is >= 0.03 on val | R2: maker round trip <= 1 bp (fees alone are ~7 bp)

claim: 1h low-entry limit bracket: 945 combos (9 entries a*pred or offset 0-0.3%, TP b, 5 stop types, 7 direction sources incl. random, always-buy, always-sell) plus buy/sell offset sweeps on all coins
cost_model: maker 0.02% entry/TP, taker 0.05% stop/exit + 0.02% stop slippage; LB (stop counted if touched, TP not counted if order unknown) and UB bounds
failure_location: net P&L under intrabar-order lower bound
evidence: best on val (-RSI, a=1, b=0.5, no stop): fill 49%, win 48.4% vs 51.8% breakeven, net -0.035%/trade (gross +0.035%), per-period -0.018% t=-3.6, 1 of 11 months positive; no combo reaches t>2 on val; controls: random direction t=-6.0, always-buy -4.9, inverted -RSI -9.4 (gross t=-2.2). UB gives t=+19..+23 even with RANDOM direction. Offset sweep: fill 96%->52%, adverse-selection gap -0.04..+0.02%, all results negative t -4.9..-11
verified_cause: the apparent upper-bound edge is intrabar ordering (random direction reproduces it); the lower bound is net negative and the direction model adds nothing over range prediction
cause_test: random-direction control gives the same UB t (+19..+23) as the model; inverted direction is also negative before fees
invariants: at 1h bars without intrabar path, fill order cannot be resolved and any limit-bracket result sits between LB<0 and UB inflated by ordering; the model contributes no direction value above range prediction
reopen_if: R1: intrabar path data (15m or finer) resolving ordering, with LB gross edge > fees (history_15m was inaccessible then) | R2: maker rebate or round trip <= 2 bp

evidence: no representation qualifies (needs +0.005 AUC in both TFs, >=7/10 coins, better net P&L): wavelet 1h +0.0064 (7/10 coins; net +2.6bp but still -6.9bp) / 4h -0.003; RQA ~0 (+0.000/-0.000); tokens -0.001 (1h) / -0.008 (4h). Token next-token cross-entropy 1h -0.56% (passes 0.5%) but decomposed: magnitude tokens 1.41% (1h)/0.97% (4h), sign tokens 0.12%/0.07% - the 'language' is volatility clustering, not direction
invariants: direction AUC gain over the baseline from tokens/wavelet/RQA is <= +0.0064; next-token predictability is volatility clustering (magnitude), not direction. Effective sample size vs feature count, feature-count sweep and learning curve not recorded
reopen_if: R1: a representation fed by information not derivable from OHLCV | R2: capacity controls run (effective samples, k-sweep, learning curve) on the combined B+T+W+R set | R3: use magnitude predictability for sizing/when-to-trade (not a direction claim)

claim: Owner's 4-output path envelope (max up U, max down Dn, close-from-low CL, close-from-high CH in ATR units; HistGBR per target) driving TP/SL trades by asymmetry
universe: 10 coins Binance spot, trades on 5m path
failure_location: directional skill of the asymmetry vs close return
evidence: magnitude outputs predictable: Spearman 0.13-0.19 vs realised (U 0.148/0.145, Dn 0.130/0.149, CL 0.187/0.183, CH 0.162/0.182 at 1h/4h), R2 vs symmetric-vol +0.015..0.03; asymmetry Spearman 0.045/0.040 vs realised U+Dn but 0.000/-0.009 vs close return; trades 1h -9.5 bp t=-6.5, 4h -0.7 bp t=-0.19 (4/10 coins; 2023-24 -3.5, 2025-26 +2.5)
invariants: envelope size is predictable from OHLCV features while direction is not (asymmetry carries no close-direction skill); effective sample size, feature-count sweep and learning curve not recorded
reopen_if: R1: envelope used for sizing/TP placement on top of an external direction source (e.g. the H07 trend filter) | R2: capacity controls run for the direction part (k-sweep k=1,3,5,10, learning curve)

claim: Direction inferred arithmetically from the 4 envelope outputs: implied closes R1=Dn+CL and R2=U+CH, their mean and their agreement
failure_location: Spearman of implied close vs realised return
evidence: implied-close Spearman vs realised return 0.014/0.002 (1h/4h) for the mean, 0.015/0.005 on agreement; R1 vs R2 correlation 0.77 (not independent); trades: 4h S +1.3 bp (t=0.38); 4h S|agree +2.1 bp (t=0.59, 5/10 coins, 2023-24 +0.2, 2025-26 +4.3; positive, not significant); 1h all -8..-11 bp
verified_cause: arithmetic on model outputs cannot create direction information absent from the inputs; the two implied closes are built from the same inputs
cause_test: implied closes correlate 0.77 with each other and 0.002-0.015 with realised return; agreement filter adds no skill
invariants: any deterministic function of the 4 envelope outputs has ~0 direction skill when the outputs carry only magnitude
reopen_if: R1: envelope outputs fed with direction-bearing inputs (an external direction source) | R2: 4h agree-variant paper-trade on future data as monitoring only

claim: Stage-2 stacking: logistic on [U,Dn,CL,CH,R1,R2,U+Dn] + entry-candle details fitted on validation 2022 only
evidence: stage-2 AUC 0.510/0.509 (1h/4h); trades 4h stage-2 -16 bp, 1h -8..-11 bp; report note: it 'memorized 2022'
invariants: stage-2 was fitted on a single year (2022) with ~13 features; effective sample size, feature-count sweep and learning curve not recorded
reopen_if: R1: stage-2 with <= k features chosen on train/val and effective samples per feature >= N | R2: capacity sweep and learning curve not yet run

claim: Owner's wick capture: sell limit at predicted high / buy limit at predicted low of the current candle (quantile GBM q 0.3/0.5/0.7), exit at candle close
cost_model: maker 0.02% entry, taker 0.05%+0.02% exit (0.09% RT), 2bp trade-through
evidence: GROSS per filled trade negative everywhere: 4h -0.8..-1.8 bp, 1h -2.6..-3.3, 15m -2.9..-3.2; net -10..-12 bp, t -9..-240, 0/10 coins; model levels ~ ATR-band baseline (no added value)
verified_cause: adverse selection: a limit at the extreme fills mostly on momentum candles and the close lands beyond the level
cause_test: reverse trade at the same levels (H23-R) has gross ~+1 bp, i.e. fade and breakout gross sum ~ -2x slippage; fills conditioned on touch show close beyond the level on average
invariants: gross P&L of fading predicted candle extremes is negative at 15m/1h/4h; ATR bands do as well as the model
reopen_if: R1: a pre-fill signal not derivable from OHLCV that separates exhaustion from momentum touches, shown with gross > 0 | R2: a rebate-based negative-fee venue is not sufficient (gross is negative)

claim: Reverse of wick capture: BUY stop at predicted high / SELL stop at predicted low, exit at close (breakout)
failure_location: net P&L; gross ~ +1 bp vs 9-14 bp cost
verified_cause: at candle extremes the market is a fair coin: fade and breakout gross sum ~ -2x slippage, so either side pays the cost without an edge
cause_test: paired fade (H23) and breakout (H23-R) runs on identical levels: gross -1..-3 bp vs +~1 bp
invariants: breakout at predicted candle extremes has gross <= ~1.3 bp (15m/1h), < cost 12-15 bp
reopen_if: R1: round trip <= 1 bp and a pre-fill signal that lifts gross above cost | R2: an information source not derivable from OHLCV

claim: ADX / NATR-percentile / ATR-ratio regime filters (plus theory combos) on wick-capture fade and breakout trades, 84 configs
evidence: 0 of 84 selected on 2022 (net>0 and t>2); best on 2022: 4h fade + ATR expanding +16.6 bp (t 1.86), + NATR high +13.5 bp (t 1.75); on 2023-26 the same configs -5.9 / -6.3 bp, 1/10 coins; theory combos worse than no filter
invariants: ADX/NATR/ATR filters measure past move size/trend strength, not which side fills profitably; high-volatility filters help the fade only because cost is a smaller share of a bigger candle (stated, not separately tested)
reopen_if: R1: a filter that conditions on the fill-side outcome (a pre-fill signal not derivable from OHLCV) | R2: cost per trade <= 1 bp

claim: Chart-image CNN (JKX style: 48x96 px OHLC + EMA20 + volume, 32-bar window) predicting direction over the next 8 (1h) / 6 (4h) bars, with sample filters C0 none, C1 ATR14/ATR100>1.2, C2 |EMA20-EMA50|>1.5 ATR14, C3 volume spike; top/bottom 20% of val p traded
universe: 10 coins Binance spot (BTC ETH SOL ADA BCH BNB DOGE TRX XRP ZEC)
failure_location: gross edge per trade vs round-trip cost, all 8 configs
evidence: net < 0 in 8/8 configs (best 1h C1 CNN -4.3bp, t -0.95, 2/10 coins); max gross +9.7bp; maker-cost best +5.7bp t<1; test AUC 0.495-0.545; CNN beats the logistic baseline on the same normalized window in 4/8 only
verified_cause: the 32-bar OHLCV window carries at most ~0.53 AUC of next-8-bar direction, worth less than the 14bp round-trip cost; the image representation adds no information over the same window as numbers
cause_test: logistic regression on the identical normalized window values, same samples/splits: same AUC (0.51-0.53) and net within noise of the CNN in every config; zero-skill check via the filters: C2 negative even before costs
invariants: gross per trade < 14bp RT in every TF x filter; direction AUC <= 0.545 from any rendering of a 32-bar OHLCV window; image vs numeric window equal within noise
reopen_if: R1: maker round trip <= 4bp with a pre-registered maker-fill model (maker_net was positive but t<1) | R2: inputs carrying information not derivable from the OHLCV window (funding/OI/order book/cross-asset) rendered or concatenated with the image | R3: a pre-registered horizon/target where gross on val exceeds 2x cost

claim: ML (HistGradientBoosting) and HAR-RV next-day realized-volatility forecasts (5m RV features) replacing the trailing 30-day std in H07 position sizing (weight 0.02/sigma, cap 3)
failure_location: sizing rule (forecast -> weight), not the forecast
evidence: VAL Sharpe trail30 0.908 vs har 0.720 [dSharpe CI -0.44,+0.09] vs gbm 0.627 [-0.57,+0.05]; maxDD -24% vs -29%/-27%; TEST agrees (0.87 / 0.86 / 0.76); forecast QLIKE better for gbm (BTC 0.41 vs 0.62, ETH 0.31 vs 0.62)
verified_cause: trend returns on held days rise with that day's volatility, so accurate next-day vol targeting cuts exposure on the days that pay
cause_test: VAL decomposition: gross Sharpe also lower (0.96 / 0.82 / 0.74) while turnover only doubles; gbm lowest-weight (highest predicted vol) tercile +38 bp/day vs +15 bp highest-weight; corr(weight, next-day return) +0.049 trail30 vs -0.006 gbm
invariants: better next-day vol forecasts (QLIKE) do not translate into better H07 Sharpe; continuous inverse-forecast-vol sizing lowers exposure on high-return volatile trend days
reopen_if: R1: a pre-registered sizing rule that uses the forecast without cutting exposure on predicted-high-vol trend days (e.g. only as a crash filter: extreme predicted vol AND trend off) | R2: a horizon matching the trend signal (multi-week vol forecast) instead of next-day

claim: Extensions of the frozen H07 trend filter: V1 multi-speed ensemble (10/20/30/60d), V2 fast exit (30d AND 10d), V3 same rule on 10 coins, V4 ensemble on 10 coins
universe: BTC ETH SOL ADA BCH BNB DOGE TRX XRP ZEC (Binance spot)
failure_location: Sharpe difference vs H07 on val (block bootstrap, Bonferroni 4 variants)
verified_cause: the improvements are smaller than the sampling uncertainty of a Sharpe difference between two correlated daily trend strategies (+-0.3-0.8 over 6 years)
cause_test: stationary block bootstrap (block 20, 2000 draws) of the paired daily Sharpe difference on VAL; Bonferroni 98.75% intervals all include 0
invariants: with ~6 years of daily data a Sharpe gain below ~0.5 cannot be separated from noise for these variants; the mechanisms (less lag, diversification) are present
reopen_if: R1: >= 12 months of forward paper trading of V3/V4 as shadow variants vs V0 (research/h07_forward), judged by the same paired bootstrap on the pooled VAL+forward period | R2: additional independent history (more coins or pre-2018 data) adding power
